steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add celery, onion, and ½ teaspoon salt; cook and stir until onion soft and brown, about 12 minutes. Stir in carrot; cook 5 minutes. Stir in apple; remove from heat.

Combine ground chicken, ⅓ cup applesauce, bread crumbs, egg, milk, poultry seasoning, sage, remaining ½ teaspoon salt, and black pepper in a bowl; mix in carrot-apple mixture until well combined. Form mixture into a loaf; place in center of a 9x12-inch baking dish.
Combine remaining ⅓ cup applesauce, Dijon mustard, and honey in a bowl; spread over top and sides of meatloaf.

Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C); continue cooking until an instant-read thermometer inserted into center reads 165 degrees F (74 degrees C), about 30 minutes more. Rest meatloaf before serving, 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Tangy Apple Chicken Loaf
raw_recipe.description: This sweet and savory chicken loaf recipe is flavored with apples, carrots, and applesauce and then painted with a tangy mustard-honey-applesauce glaze.

review.reviewBody: This is the best meat loaf I have ever eaten. The only thing that I changed was the chicken, I used turkey. Very moist. Tried this out on my boyfriend and he went back twice for more. He couldn't wait for leftovers tonight. It was better tonight. Tanks for the WONDERFUL healthy recipe.

Made it again tonight, but I had to make double so there would be leftovers. This time, after I sautéed the onions, carrots and apples, I deglazed the pan with 2 oz. of Jack Daniels Apple. I also add 2 tsp. of Roasted Chicken - Better Than Bouillon. Otherwise, I pretty much follow the recipe as is (though I do use fresh herbs from my garden).

Other than lining my pan with parchment paper to make cleanup easier and subbing Quaker Oats for the breadcrumbs, as another reviewer did, to make this gluten free, I followed the recipe exactly, and it came out perfect and delicious! My son sprinkled a little hot sauce on his and thought that made it even better. The rest of us liked it just as well without the hot sauce.

I followed this pretty close but madea few adjusstments. I used olive oil instead of butter, omitted the applesauce in the meat misture as well as the sage. I used a muffin pan and I made 6 large heaping muffin sized loafs and with the little bit of extra meat I made meatballs (they were very good!). As for the sauce I used a maple mustard I had bougth (similar to a honey mustard) and instead of honey I used maple syrup. The meat was great without it but the sauce gave it an extra boost of yumminess!! I glazed the meat as per direction but I had leftovers which I spooned over the meat on my plate and it was great! Thank you for this great recipe!!

EDIT: The meatballs I made with this were great by themselves but are also great with pasta or a thai/plum sauce kind of thing! Thanks again!

This was delicious! My husband loved it, and I will definitely make it again. I made a few minor changes. I only used about 2 tablespoons of chopped onion, and about 1 stalk of celery. I left out the pepper (my husband hates pepper), and the sage. The poultry seasoning I used already had quite a bit of sage in it, so I didn't want to overdo it. I used 1 cup of breadcrumbs instead of 1/2 cup. The mixture was too 'wet' with only 1/2 cup. Lastly, I didn't use mustard for the glaze. I'm not a big fan of mustard. So I substituted it with 2 tablespoons of Jack Daniel's Honey Smokehouse BBQ sauce instead (I'm sure any BBQ would do). It took an extra 10 minutes or so in my oven for the center to reach 180 degrees. I served it with homemade mashed potatoes and green beans. It was fabulous!

Wow! I would have deducted a star for presentation had the taste not made up for it. This was delicious. My husband said, "like stuffing, but better". We enjoy sweet tastes, so this was perfect. So kid friendly, too. Made a couple of changes based on what I had and would repeat them again: no celery, used a mild zucchini like squash instead, sweet vidalia onion, ran all veggies through food processor and cooked at the same time in butter for at least 15 minutes (no chunks here), increased sauce and added more honey to taste (my mustard was very strong & my applesauce was unsweetened.) Used only sage, marjoram, thyme, & rosemary, as we are not fond of nutmeg or ginger that is typically in poultry seasoning. Fabulous. Our toddler said "mmmmm" and danced when I brought out the leftovers. Had to add much more breadcrumbs, but my crumbs were very fine. Set oven for 400 and reduced to 380 when I put the loaf in. (Wanted to walk away for more than 1/2 hour). Will do again and again, maybe with turkey and better bread crumbs. Possibly will experiment with individual portions for improved appearance. Thank you so very much. A lean chicken dish filled with veggies that everyone loves? 5 stars plus!

This was delicious. What a great way to use ground chicken. I normally use this in place of ground chuck, so a new way to use it was welcome. I used a little rosemary, thyme and white pepper since I didn't have poultry spice. I also doubled the sauce and was glad I did because there wasn't a lot despite doubling. I added little red potatoes to the pan with the loaf. Had some yellow squash on the side. We'll have this again, thanks for sharing!

OH EM GEE so good. Another reviewer already said this but this loaf tastes like Turkey Dinner on thanksgiving. Soooooo good. My husband liked it and he has some weird aversion to any fruit being cooked in his food. The ingredients sounds weird but tastes so good together. The only changes I made were 1) had no sage so put herbs de provence in instead; 2) put 1/2 cup of oatmeal in because the mix was too wet. Otherwise followed the recipe exactly.

This was not bad. My picky daughter liked it more than I did. She did suggest a different sauce for the top. 

1 cup Un-sweetened applesauce, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 TBS bbq sauce, t TBS Worcestershire sauce, and 1 cove garlic

Also, maybe a little red pepper flake to add some kick.

Delicate flavors. Next time I will increase the spices a bit, but this was lovely. Served with extra applesauce on the side.
I made this (minus the applesauce) because I didn't have it. I loved it. I'm sure the applesauce would make it even better.

I really liked this recipe overall. Like most, some things I had to tweak due to what I had. I added 1/2 lb. of turkey to my 1 lb of chicken. Didn't have poultry seasoning, so used herb de provence. Didn't have an apple, so just stuck with the apple sauce. Used saltines instead of bread crumbs and didn't add the salt. Had the rest of the ingredients and followed it. I did throw in in some fennel seed(which I wouldn't next time, was trying to add a sausageness to it) and garlic powder. It has good flavor overall. I will use an apple next time to help with the moisture and will try cooking it in a loaf pan instead of 9x13. Love the glaze.
This was easy to make and a really good blend of flavors. I will make it again and definitely worth a try for something delicious and different!
Absolutely wonderful as written- no changes needed! This makes a BIG loaf but you could easily cut it down! I plan to freeze some! Thank you!
Made it with ground beef. Delicious !
This recipe is excellent as is, I didn't need to change a thing. It has become a household staple meal replacing my mother's meatloaf.

I love this recipe and have made it several times. However, the first time I found the glaze somewhat blasé, so since then I make a tangier one using ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, mirin( rice wine), honey, low sodium soy sauce, finely grated ginger and freshly ground black pepper. Everyone who has ever eaten this raves about it. Thank you for the baseline recipe.
